correctness.rationale: At every clique vertex, all path color classes have odd global multiplicity, while path-neighbor parity forces unequal colors at distance two; properness forces distance one. Clique colors are distinct and disjoint from path colors. Thus a strong-odd coloring is exactly a path word with gaps ≥3 between identical symbols and every used class odd, plus r clique colors. For 1≤n≤6 a repeated class would require at least three occurrences spanning ≥7 positions, so all letters distinct. For n≥7, three colors force ABCABC… and are all odd precisely at n≡3(mod6); color-class oddness forces palette parity to agree with n. Explicit admissible seeds of lengths 3,4,5,7,8,12 and prefix block 012012 supply the sharp 3/4/5 upper bounds for every residue class. Independently checked parity-state minimal word palettes for path orders 1..36; finite checks corroborate the all-length combinatorial argument.
residual_risks: Formula is for clique–path joins with r,n≥1, not general graph joins.
Finite enumeration cannot prove the unbounded six-periodic theorem independently of constructions and lower bounds.
